as_told.title: Documentary clip: binary model explains celestial observations

plain: This story is about a documentary film called The Great Year. It deals with a long, slow cycle in the sky known by that name. A researcher on ancient history named Matt LaCroix describes it on a podcast with the host Jesse Michels. He says the film's makers proposed that the Great Year comes from our Sun moving in a pair with a partner star, and that they thought this partner was Sirius, a bright star. A clip of the documentary's own narrator is played in the same episode. The narrator says some believe this paired-star model fits everything we see in the sky. He adds that it does so without needing extra twisting forces or epicycles, the small added circles once used to explain how planets move. If true, it would change how we picture the Sun's place among the stars.
